slot.brief: A statement about what happens to equilibrium position/K when pressure or inert gas is added or temperature changed; pick correct effect on K and yield

stem: For the exothermic equilibrium $\text{N}_2(g)+3\text{H}_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2\text{NH}_3(g)$, which change increases the equilibrium yield of $\text{NH}_3$?
options: Increasing the pressure at constant temperature
Increasing the temperature at constant pressure
Adding an inert gas at constant volume
notes: from question bank g4e2d368b1b98 (verified in job 20261127-141153-3072)
working:
Reactant side: $4$ mol gaseous species; product side: $2$ mol.\nIncreasing pressure shifts equilibrium toward fewer gas moles: $\text{NH}_3$ yield increases.

Independent check: Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium toward the side with fewer gas moles: 2 mol NH₃ versus 4 mol reactants. Thus NH₃ yield increases.
solution:
By Le Chatelier’s principle, increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium toward the side with fewer gaseous moles.
$$4\text{ mol reactants} > 2\text{ mol NH}_3$$
Hence, the equilibrium yield of NH₃ increases.
